articles.title: Sustaining livelihoods amid crisis in Gaza
articles.summary: Nidaa, Hanaa and Hanin have different stories, but share a common thread: the determination to build something of their own and keep it going despite extraordinary challenges facing them in war-ravaged Gaza.
articles.content:
Following the devastation of the past three years, productive capacity in Gaza has been severely damaged, markets disrupted and the cost of basic goods has risen sharply.

Their experiences reflect different parts of the same challenge: sustaining livelihoods that still exist, helping businesses restart and creating new opportunities where livelihoods have disappeared.

Running a business today means navigating uncertainty at every turn. Yet amid these challenges, women continue to find ways to work, adapting their businesses, learning new skills and somehow – supporting their families.

Nidaa: A livelihood built from childhood

Nidaa, 35, has her own business raising and selling chickens, ducks and rabbits in the southern city of Khan Younis.

“I was passionate about this business since I was a child,” she said. “My mother worked with animals, and she taught me everything she knew. During the war, I faced many challenges with continuing my business. However, I insisted on continuing.”

When her home was destroyed during the war and she was displaced, she managed to save some of her animals and move them to Khan Younis.

Trained as a teacher, Nidaa chose to follow her passion for raising animals, turning it into a business that helps support her family, including two brothers with disabilities. But there have been constant challenges.

‘During the time of famine, I lost many animals’

“Especially during the time of famine, I lost many animals,” she recalled. “Food became very expensive.”

Right now, challenges include shelter for the coming winter, access to safe water and limited ingredients for food for the birds and animals, she said.

“I don’t know how I will take care of them without a proper shelter,” she said.

Through the UN Development Programme (UNDP) partnership with the local Chamber of Commerce, she received a grant to purchase animals and equipment, alongside training to strengthen her production skills.

Now, Nidaa’s ambition goes beyond sustaining what she has today.

“I hope that my business will grow,” she said, “and I can inspire other women to work with animals.”

© UNDP

Hanaa: Starting again after loss

In Gaza City, Hanaa, 49, started a family dairy business with her husband in 2021.

During the war, she lost her husband, one of her sons and her business. She was left supporting her three remaining children while also caring for five children who lost both parents.

With encouragement from her eldest son, Fouad, Hanaa decided to restart the business despite limited resources and severe shortages of milk and other raw materials.

“Sometimes, the people who need us are the reason we find the strength to keep going,” Hanaa said, adding that she chooses to remain strong and resilient in the face of many challenges.

The destruction of Gaza’s electricity system has made dairy production particularly difficult. Power interruptions can cause products to spoil, resulting in losses at a time when resources are already scarce.

With grant support, Hanaa was able to resume producing cheese, milk, labneh and laban, with hopes of growing her business into a larger production facility and build a more stable source of income for her family.

Hanin: Learning a new trade

For other women, starting over begins with a new skill.

Hanin, 36, is learning carpentry. From southern Khan Younis, she travels to Deir al-Balah to complete 80 hours of vocational training, followed by entrepreneurship and business-planning training.

“This is something unique, especially for women,” Hanin said. “It’s needed now more than ever, because there are limited sources of wood for furniture, and many people lost their furniture during the war.”

More than 200 trainees will receive skills development in carpentry, textiles, recycling, compost production, data science, graphic design and digital marketing.

For Hanin, learning carpentry is not simply about completing a training course. It offers a pathway towards earning an income and potentially building a business of her own.

© UNDP

Foundations for the future

For women entrepreneurs, access to finance and skills is important, but their ability to sustain and grow their businesses also depends on the systems around them.

That means reliable energy and water, functioning markets and access to the equipment and materials they need.

Supporting women-led businesses is therefore about more than individual livelihoods, according to UNDP.

It also helps preserve local productive capacity, generate income and keep economic activity rooted in Palestinian communities, laying the foundation for locally driven recovery.

articles.reasoning: The article highlights the resilience and determination of women in Gaza to sustain and rebuild their livelihoods despite severe challenges caused by war and economic disruption. It details real-world impact through UNDP-supported initiatives that provide grants, training, and skills development, enabling women to restart or start businesses, which benefits families and the broader community. The story is focused, detailed, and significant for the general public as it reflects broader themes of economic recovery, empowerment, and local resilience in a conflict-affected region.
articles.personality_title: Women in Gaza rebuild businesses despite war challenges
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Gaza has faced severe damage to its economy and daily life due to war over the past three years. Many businesses have closed, and basic goods have become expensive. Women in Gaza are working hard to keep their livelihoods alive amid this difficult situation.

**What happened** – Three women, Nidaa, Hanaa, and Hanin, show how they are rebuilding their businesses or learning new skills. Nidaa raises chickens and rabbits, continuing her family tradition even after losing her home. Hanaa restarted a dairy business after losing family members and her original business in the war. Hanin is learning carpentry, a new skill, to start a business in a field with growing need. Support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) helped them with grants, training, and supplies.

**Impact** – These stories show how women in Gaza are adapting to survive and support their families. Their efforts help keep local markets alive and create jobs, which is important where many people have lost everything. The projects also help preserve skills and build hope for economic recovery in their communities.

**What's next step** – The women plan to grow their businesses and inspire others. More training programs are underway to teach skills like carpentry and digital marketing to over 200 people. Continued support for energy, water, and markets will be needed to help these businesses succeed long term.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Despite war and hardship, women in Gaza are rebuilding their businesses and skills with UN support, helping their families and communities recover.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des femmes à Gaza reconstruisent leurs entreprises malgré la guerre
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Gaza a subi de lourds dégâts économiques et sociaux à cause de la guerre ces trois dernières années. Beaucoup d’entreprises ont fermé et les produits de première nécessité sont devenus chers. Des femmes à Gaza s’efforcent de préserver leurs moyens de subsistance dans ces conditions difficiles.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Trois femmes, Nidaa, Hanaa et Hanin, montrent comment elles reconstruisent leur activité ou apprennent un nouveau métier. Nidaa élève des poulets et des lapins, poursuivant une tradition familiale malgré la perte de sa maison. Hanaa a relancé une entreprise laitière après avoir perdu des proches et son commerce pendant la guerre. Hanin apprend la menuiserie pour créer un nouveau métier dans un secteur en demande. Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) leur a apporté des subventions, des formations et du matériel.

**Impact** – Ces histoires montrent comment ces femmes s’adaptent pour survivre et soutenir leur famille. Leurs efforts maintiennent les marchés locaux et créent des emplois, ce qui est crucial dans une région où beaucoup ont tout perdu. Ces projets préservent aussi des compétences et ouvrent des perspectives pour la reprise économique.

**Prochaines étapes** – Ces femmes souhaitent développer leurs entreprises et encourager d’autres femmes. Plus de 200 personnes suivent des formations en menuiserie, marketing digital et autres métiers. Un soutien continu en énergie, eau et marchés est nécessaire pour assurer la réussite durable des entreprises.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Malgré la guerre et les difficultés, des femmes à Gaza reconstruisent leurs entreprises et apprennent de nouveaux savoir-faire grâce au soutien de l’ONU, aidant leurs familles et leurs communautés à se relever.
articles.personality_title_es: Mujeres en Gaza reconstruyen negocios a pesar de la guerra
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Gaza ha sufrido graves daños económicos y sociales debido a la guerra en los últimos tres años. Muchos negocios cerraron y los productos básicos se volvieron caros. Mujeres en Gaza trabajan duro para mantener sus medios de vida en esta difícil situación.

**Qué pasó** – Tres mujeres, Nidaa, Hanaa y Hanin, muestran cómo están reconstruyendo sus negocios o aprendiendo nuevas habilidades. Nidaa cría pollos y conejos, continuando una tradición familiar a pesar de perder su hogar. Hanaa reinició un negocio de productos lácteos tras perder a familiares y su negocio durante la guerra. Hanin está aprendiendo carpintería para iniciar un negocio en un área con demanda creciente. El Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) les brindó apoyo con subvenciones, capacitación y materiales.

**Impacto** – Estas historias muestran cómo las mujeres en Gaza se adaptan para sobrevivir y apoyar a sus familias. Sus esfuerzos ayudan a mantener los mercados locales y crear empleos, algo vital en una zona donde muchos lo han perdido todo. Los proyectos también preservan habilidades y abren esperanza para la recuperación económica.

**Próximo paso** – Las mujeres planean hacer crecer sus negocios e inspirar a otras. Más de 200 personas están recibiendo formación en carpintería, marketing digital y otras áreas. Se necesita seguir apoyando la energía, el agua y los mercados para que estos negocios tengan éxito a largo plazo.

**Resumen en una frase** – A pesar de la guerra y las dificultades, mujeres en Gaza reconstruyen sus negocios y aprenden nuevas habilidades con apoyo de la ONU, ayudando a sus familias y comunidades a recuperarse.
